headline: Tech stocks hit records early last week, then fell, with AI shares hit hardest by doubts over OpenAI's revenue, before rebounding on Friday, says the Investing News Network's weekly recap.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 1: this recaps events of 5 to 9 Oct 2026 that earlier editions already carried; read in full but not new.
importance_line: What changed is that one week showed AI-linked shares swinging on reports about OpenAI's revenue and on worries over how the build-out is financed, which matters first to savers whose pensions and index funds hold these shares, then to investors and lenders funding the build-out, and the doubt is that the moves rest on reports the companies have not confirmed.
summary: The Investing News Network's weekly tech recap reports that the Nasdaq closed at records on 5 and 6 Oct 2026, fell 1.25% on 8 Oct, when chip and AI stocks were hit hardest after the Financial Times reported that OpenAI's revenue was well below the figure widely circulated, and rebounded on 9 Oct after Bloomberg reported that OpenAI expects its yearly revenue pace to reach $70 billion or more by the end of 2026. It adds that questions are growing over how the AI build-out is being paid for, citing reports that Amazon, Oracle and Nvidia are tapping debt markets and that Broadcom is lining up financing for Anthropic and OpenAI chips, which none of the companies have confirmed.
notes: CNBC Investing Club's own recap is blocked (HTTP 403), so the entry credits the Investing News Network's weekly recap of the same week. The link is a rolling page that is replaced each week. Older news re-dated: the OpenAI revenue scare was carried in our 9 Oct 2026 edition and the $70 billion report in the 10 Oct edition.
